{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Licence Agreement — verified findings 

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Six clauses are compliant and require no redline; ten are deviations that fail the applicable fallback, and two rules are unaddressed entirely (post-termination transition/data return, and Vendor insurance).

The risk profile is heavily one-sided. Three critical items sit together and compound each other: the only indemnity in the Agreement runs from us to the Licensor (Article XII) while Article XIII expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement; the liability cap protects the Licensor alone and at one half of amounts paid, leaving us uncapped; and Article III vests ownership of the bespoke customization we commission and pay for — including our unique client front end — in the Licensor, with no assignment to us and no licence-back beyond the 36-month term. We also have no exit: no termination for convenience, a Licensor-option seven-year renewal, and no obligation on the Licensor to return our data or support a migration, against a Change of Control clause that auto-terminates our licences.

On the positive side, the commercial construct is clean where it matters most to the business: pricing is purely usage-based with no minimum commitment or take-or-pay, there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN or Customer-payable liquidated damages, and governing law and venue (New York; exclusive New York state and federal courts) are at our preferred position.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Arts. XII, XIII) | One-way Licensee indemnity; no Licensor IP indemnity and an express disclaimer of infringement liability. Add Licensor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and narrow our indemnity to Licensee content and our breach. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. III) | Licensor owns all additions, improvements and Derivative Works, including paid-for customization; no data ownership statement. Add Licensee ownership of paid-for deliverables with perpetual licence to embedded Licensor IP, plus Licensee Data ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Art. XIII) | Cap and consequential-damages exclusion run only in Licensor's favour, at one half of amounts paid, with no carve-outs. Make mutual, cap at greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, carve out Excluded Claims. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (Arts. XX(a), XXII) | Blanket bar on our assignment, none on Licensor's, plus automatic termination on our Change of Control. Add affiliate/successor carve-out, restrict Licensor assignment, remove the change-of-control termination. Licensor's right of first refusal over our M&A noted for the exit workstream. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Arts. II, IV) | Grant limited to Licensee employees; Affiliates and contractors excluded and no successor transfer. Extend grant to Affiliates and contractors and permit transfer to an M&A successor. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV) | 36-month term with no Licensee convenience right. Add 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. | Licence is non-exclusive throughout; no sole-source or requirements obligation. Preferred position met. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No LDs, penalties or early-termination charges; Art. XXIII bars termination damages against either party. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. | Article II restrictions are IP scope limits on the licensed software, not restraints on our business. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV) | Unilateral Licensor option to extend by seven years, no opt-out, no uplift cap. Replace with 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Pure AS IS with no conformance warranty and no remedy. Add 12-month conformance, workmanlike-services, legal-compliance and no-malicious-code warranties with repair/replace/refund, carved out of the disclaimer; 90 days is the fallback. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Art. XXI) | Article XXI is one-directional: we return everything in five days, with no Licensor obligation to return or export our data. Insert up to six months' assistance, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion; 90 days' assistance is the fallback. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Art. X(b)) | One-way, Term plus three years, covering the entire Licensor and Affiliate workforce. Make mutual, limit to personnel directly involved in the services, cut tail to 12 months from end of involvement. Existing advertising/unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs retained. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | "50+ US$5.00" (Art. II, Record Keeping and Reports (b)) | No frequency cap and no minimum notice. Add once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor, no system access. Cost-shifting above a 5% discrepancy is already at our preferred position and is untouched. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (Art. XXIV(a)) | New York law with exclusive New York state and federal courts; no arbitration. Venue stated as the City of New York rather than New York County — de minimis, noted only. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | "50+ US$5.00" | No MFN obligation on us; the only third-party comparison (Revisions on general release) runs in our favour. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. V) | Purely usage-based pricing; volume bands operate as a discount, not a floor. No minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions | No coverage covenant at all, despite the Licensor hosting the Platform and handling our data. Insert an insurance paragraph as General Provisions (l) with certificates on request; fallback limits E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following deviations are identified in the findings as walk-away territory (or, for insurance, as approaching it) and should not be conceded without a business decision at principal level:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity** (Arts. XII, XIII), aggravated by the express disclaimer of liability for third-party IP infringement claims.
2. **Licensor-only liability cap at one half of amounts paid**, with us uncapped, no super-cap and no confidentiality/indemnity/gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs (Art. XIII).
3. **Ownership of paid-for customization and Derivative Works vesting in the Licensor**, with no assignment and no perpetual licence-back, and no statement of our data rights (Art. III).
4. **Blanket assignment bar on us with automatic termination of all licences on our Change of Control**, while the Licensor may assign freely (Arts. XX(a), XXII).
5. **No Licensee termination for convenience** in a 36-month term.
6. **Licensor-option seven-year renewal** with no opt-out and no pricing cap (Art. IV).
7. **Pure AS IS supply** with no conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy (Art. VIX).
8. **No post-termination transition assistance or return of our data**, against a five-day return-and-certify obligation on us (Art. XXI).
9. **Uncapped audit frequency** with no minimum notice (Art. II, Record Keeping and Reports (b)).
10. **Three-year, whole-workforce, one-way non-solicit** binding us (Art. X(b)).
11. **No insurance covenant of any kind** for a hosted trading platform handling our data.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten deviations and two missing clauses, with playbook comments (prefix `[Playbook]`) explaining the change and the fallback where one is available.
2. **Lead negotiation with the critical cluster** — Licensor IP indemnity, mutual cap with carve-outs, and ownership of the customization we pay for — and treat them as linked; the infringement disclaimer in Article XIII must be reconciled with the new indemnity.
3. **Open a second front on exit rights**: convenience termination, the renewal mechanic, the change-of-control auto-termination, and transition assistance/data return. These are interdependent and should be traded as a package.
4. **Confirm business inputs**: acceptable cap level and any appetite for the 12-month fee fallback; whether 90 days' transition assistance suffices; Affiliates and contractors requiring Platform access; and confirmation of the Licensor's existing E&O and cyber coverage before we settle limits.
5. **Flag for the corporate team** the Article XXII right of first refusal over a sale of our assets or a change of control, which we have noted rather than redlined under the assignment rule.
6. **Leave the compliant items alone** — exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, governing law, MFN and minimum commitments — so that negotiating capital is spent on the walk-away list."}
